newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-D.C. UNITED RALLY TO EDGE TAMPA BAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-D.C. UNITED RALLY TO EDGE TAMPA BAY.

text.p: Nigerian Ben Iroha scored with 10 minutes remaining in the game to cap a second-half comeback from a two-goal deficit to give D.C. United a 3-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Mutiny in Major League Soccer on Sunday.

Roy Lassiter, last year's scoring champion, and Brazilian Gilmar had given the Mutiny (9-9) a 2-0 advantage. But United (13-4), the Eastern Conference leaders, rallied behind goals from John Maessner and former U.S. international Roy Wegerle, acquired in a trade with Colorado earlier in the week.
The victory further solidified United's hold on first place, following a 3-2 decision over the Dallas Burn on Friday.

El Salvadoran international Raul Diaz Arce scored for a record seventh consecutive match, in the 74th minute, to break a 2-2 tie and give United the win over Dallas. Iroha and Tony Sanneh also had goals for the winners, while Argentine Daniel Peinado and Mexican Damian Alvarez scored for the Burn (9-9).

In Kansas City, the Burn rebounded from that loss with a 3-1 victory over the Western Conference leading Kansas City Wizards (12-6), on Sunday as Jorge Rodriguez struck twice in the second half. Defender Ryan Tinsley added a goal, while Swiss international Alain Sutter tallied for the Burn.

In San Jose, El Salvadoran international Ronald Cerritos broke a 2-2 tie in the 71st minute to lift the San Jose Clash (7-11) to a 3-2 triumph over the New England Revolution (10-7). Jeff Baicher and Troy Dayak found the back of the net for the Clash, while Argentine Alberto Naveda and U.S. National Team defender Alexi Lalas scored for the Revolution.

In Friday's action, Zimbabwean international Digitial Takawira connected for a goal in each half as Kansas City recorded their fourth successive win, a 2-1 victory over hosts Columbus Crew (7-9). Peter Marino cut the lead in half for the Crew, who have lost seven of their last eight games.

Both starting goalkeepers were ejected. Kansas City keeper Mike Ammann was red-carded for kicking defender Mike Lapper in the 87th minute and his Columbus counterpart, Brad Friedel, was sent off for taking down Mark Chung on a breakaway only two minutes later. Wizards coach Ron Newman also was red-carded for an altercation with Lapper in the 90th minute.

In Denver, Paul Bravo scored twice within a 10-minute span midway through the second half against his former team to boost the vastly improved Colorado Rapids (9-9) over San Jose, 3-1. Former U.S. National Team captain Peter Vermes also scored for the Rapids, Ron Cerritos for San Jose.

In Pasadena, U.S. National Team midfielder Cobi Jones and Brazilian Welton scored late goals to lift the Los Angeles Galaxy (5-11) to a 2-0 win over New England before 59,704, the largest crowd in the league this season.
In Tampa, Lassiter's 37th-minute goal was all Tampa Bay needed in a 1-0 victory over the New York/New Jersey MetroStars (5-11), who dropped their fifth consecutive match.
